## Verdict
needs-revision

## Concerns
- Claim-4 is plausibly established by generation plus the integral no-syzygy theorem, with partition conjugation giving the right-family basis.
- Claim-5 is unsupported: no identities in \(A_+J\) prove the asserted congruences or diagonal transition.
- No degreewise ordering of the ten classes is actually specified, so the displayed matrix is not yet well-defined.
- The draft correctly states that the requested target is **not established**, since the explicit transition remains missing.

## Unresolved certificates
- [proof-attempt] In the degreewise order
  \[
  \varnothing;\ (1);\ (2),(1,1);\ (3),(2,1);\ (3,1),(2,2);\ (3,2);\ (3,3),
  \]
  prove for every \(\rho\subseteq3^2\) an exact identity
  \[
  R_{\rho'}-(-1)^{|\rho|}L_\rho
  =\sum_k a_kh_{t_k}\bar s_{\lambda_k},
  \qquad 1\le t_k\le5,\quad \bar s_{\lambda_k}\in J,
  \]
  or provide equivalent exact quotient-coordinate witnesses. These must establish the claimed transition
  \(\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,I_2,-I_2,I_2,-1,1)\).
